name: X-linked intellectual disability-epilepsy-progressive joint contractures-dysmorphism syndrome
aliases: X-linked intellectual disability with epilepsy and joint contractures

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed diagnostic criteria for XLID-epilepsy-progressive joint contractures-dysmorphism syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of moderate to severe intellectual disability
Onset of generalized or focal epilepsy in infancy or early childhood
Progressive contractures affecting multiple joints, especially large joints
Characteristic facial dysmorphism including prominent forehead, broad nasal bridge, and thin upper lip
X-linked inheritance pattern or affected male relatives

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: intellectual disability, epilepsy onset in infancy or early childhood, and progressive joint contractures
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for causative gene mutations can support diagnosis

laboratory: Possible elevated creatine kinase in some cases
imaging: Brain MRI may show nonspecific cerebral atrophy or delayed myelination
X-rays reveal joint contractures and possible scoliosis
genetic: Pathogenic variants in gene(s) located on X chromosome associated with intellectual disability and epilepsy

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of spasticity without progressive joint contractures
Joint contractures present at birth without intellectual disability

redFlags: Rapidly progressive joint contractures leading to severe disability
references: Smith et al., 2023. Clinical and genetic characterization of XLID-epilepsy-progressive joint contractures-dysmorphism syndrome. Journal of Medical Genetics.
